stop_stealing_chips_119.text:
As co-author of the original CHIPS Act, I have continuously led efforts to secure America’s technological future and to rip and replace vulnerable Chinese telecom equipment from our networks.

Recent attempts to smuggle $160 million in advanced AI chips shows a quickly evolving threat—and we need strong tools to stop theft at the source.

This week, I joined my colleagues to introduce the Stop Stealing Our Chips Act, to empower and protect whistleblowers and crack down on illegal exports.

America’s AI leadership is too important to lose. We are acting now to protect it.

https://t.co/jH2BAV5cDg

deepseek.reason: She says she joined colleagues to introduce the Stop Stealing Our Chips Act to protect whistleblowers and crack down on illegal exports.
deepseek.confidence_reason: The bill is named and she describes joining its introduction.

export_controls.text:
As co-author of the CHIPS Act, I know how critical this policy is to strengthen our national security and technological leadership.

But @realDonaldTrump threatened to abandon this once-in-a-generation effort to bring advanced semiconductor manufacturing back to America AND his #tariffs are driving up costs for what we need to be competitive in AI, including aluminum, steel, semiconductors, and electronics.

Yet another example of this Administration’s harmful chaos and uncertainty.

deepseek.reason: The statement discusses CHIPS Act manufacturing and tariff costs, not export controls.
deepseek.confidence_reason: No export-control restriction or enforcement is mentioned.

The investments in the CHIPS Act are enhancing domestic semiconductor manufacturing & bringing production back to America. These efforts will help us deploy AI & lead in the technology of the future. https://t.co/m73kdp5TaV

embedded_ivos.text: This order would block states from responding to real, evolving risks. At the same time, it’s a gift to big tech—stripping away accountability when AI is becoming more powerful and deeply embedded in people’s lives. There’s a reason Congress dismissed this approach—it’s bad policy. I’ll keep pushing back against this overreach and defend states’ ability to put meaningful protections in place.

deepseek.reason: The statement criticizes an order preempting state AI regulation, not embedded independent auditors in AI labs.
deepseek.confidence_reason: No reference to independent auditors or internal lab access.

ai_action_plan_2025.text: We are deeply concerned about the impacts of President Trump’s AI Action Plan and the executive orders announced yesterday.

deepseek.reason: The speaker says they are deeply concerned about the AI Action Plan's impacts, signaling opposition.
deepseek.confidence_reason: The statement is negative toward the plan but does not explicitly call for rejection.

ai_action_plan_2025.text: We are also alarmed by the absence of regulatory structure in this AI Action Plan to ensure the responsible development, deployment, or use of AI models, and the apparent targeting of state-level regulations. As AI is integrated with daily life and tech leaders develop more powerful models, such as Artificial General Intelligence, responsible innovation must go hand in hand with appropriate safety guardrails. In the absence of any meaningful federal alternative, our states are taking the lead in embracing common-sense safeguards to protect the public, build consumer trust, and ensure innovation and competition can continue to thrive. We are deeply concerned that the AI Action Plan would open the door to forcing states to forfeit their ability to protect the public from the escalating risks of AI, by jeopardizing states’ ability to access critical federal funding. And instead of providing a sorely needed federal regulatory framework that promotes safe model development, deployment, and use, Trump’s plan simultaneously limits states and creates a ‘wild west’ for tech companies, giving them free rein to develop and deploy models with no accountability.

deepseek.reason: The speaker criticizes the plan for lacking regulatory structure and creating a 'wild west,' arguing against it.
deepseek.confidence_reason: The statement explicitly condemns multiple features of the plan.

national_ai_framework_2026.text:
Through Trump’s AI Executive Order and now National AI Policy Framework, the administration has been bending over backwards to strip states of the ability to enact commonsense AI safeguards—all while there are no meaningful federal protections in place.
 
As Ranking Member of the Communications and Technology Subcommittee, I won’t let the Administration weaponize broadband funding to bully states out of enforcing their AI laws. That’s why my colleagues and I are introducing the GUARDRAILS Act to stop this overreach and protect the public.

https://t.co/TMpHdzAT1c

deepseek.reason: The speaker criticizes the National AI Policy Framework as stripping states of AI safeguards and introduces a bill to stop its overreach.
deepseek.confidence_reason: The statement explicitly names and criticizes the framework.
